prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
On February 28, the United States and Israel began air strikes on Iran. What followed was not a quick return to peace. It became a cycle: pressure on ships, a short pause, and pressure again.

The United States began a blockade, stopping or checking ships, on April 13. In June, the two sides agreed to a written plan to pause the fighting, and the blockade was lifted on June 18. But the pause did not last. The blockade returned in July after Iran attacked three merchant ships outside approved routes.

By August, the cost was reaching deeper into the economy. The US Navy worked to remove possible mines in the Strait of Hormuz and found more than 100 objects believed to be mines. One report from an Iranian opposition media outlet also described an oil-chemical plant stopping production and a major loss in Iran’s ability to produce natural gas. That report comes from a political source, so it needs caution.

Diplomacy was not bringing a clear way out. On August 18, President Trump said there were no talks planned with Iran. The 60-day negotiation period then ended without an agreement. A private political risk company moved its expected time for easing from September to the end of the year.

This is why the conflict now looks less like a short battle and more like a long economic drain. One assessment said the region was returning to a dangerous and difficult military stalemate, where neither side had found a clear way out.

But the evidence is not all moving in one direction. One recent US statement pointed to a strong rise in oil traffic through the strait. Official quarterly data showed a much deeper fall over the wider period. The real question is whether the latest rise can last.

【Point One】
On September 1, more than 17 million barrels a day crossed the strait, according to the US energy secretary. That was far above the energy agency’s second-quarter average of 4.9 million, but still below the prewar average of about 20 to 22 million. With no later quarterly average yet, it shows a surge in access, not proven normal shipping. The key question is whether high traffic can last.

【Point Two】
The June agreement did not create a lasting system to keep ships moving. After Iran attacked three merchant ships outside approved routes in July, the blockade returned on July 14. Later, talks were not scheduled, and the 60-day period ended without an agreement. A political pause, by itself, could not guarantee predictable trade.
